authored_by: build session (Opus), by hand, before any digest was generated
conclusions: More photoreceptors does not mean richer colour perception: mantis shrimp, with 16 receptor types, discriminate similar colours worse than humans do, because the brain architecture behind the eye determines what is perceived.

A wave cannot be focused by an aperture smaller than its wavelength (the diffraction limit), which is why a biological eye cannot focus radio and why radio astronomy uses aperture-synthesis interferometry instead.

Sensory substitution is established and working — the vOICe and BrainPort are real devices, and the visual cortex is recruited to process substitute signals — so a brain could in principle learn to perceive radar as spatial data.

The assistant marked which parts of its account were established science and which were its own extrapolation, after the user said they could not verify any of it: the 20-50x brain-size estimate was invented, and the alien eye designs and the experiential descriptions were flagged as speculation.
The user stated Seshat's raison d'etre: a dynamic teacher and collaborator that turns conversations into future structured learning sessions, not a smart assistant.

A five-layer pedagogical architecture was proposed: conversation-to-knowledge extraction, a learning model weighting what needs reinforcement, spaced repetition with active recall, thread-pulling over a concept graph, and cross-thread correlation.
Seshat today has conversation memory, session search and artifacts, but no pedagogical layer that tracks what was understood, what needs revisiting, and which threads connect.
Left open: three practical first steps were offered — a structured learning profile, a closing-ritual lesson extract, and the user naming their domains — and none was chosen.
